feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. Evidence: iteration 3 (y = 0.07, 16 mm, wheel_track 0.12) gave 54.90, with oval progress flat at 0.1175 and max_error at the 0.06 floor, while the s-bend reached 0.165 with oscillation 0.144 and the slalom had one line loss at 0.1075 progress. Iteration 2 (y = 0.04, same footprint) left oval progress at 0.115, so the lead, not the footprint, moved the s-bend and slalom. Integration note: I kept the controller unchanged, so the same kp now produces about 20% more yaw (0.12/0.10). That is the effect you want on the oval, but it is also the main risk on the s-bend. Decide the next step from the race telemetry: if the oval rises above 0.1175 with max_error below 0.06 and the s-bend oscillation stays at or below 0.15, the turn-authority hypothesis holds and the next test is the lead. If the s-bend oscillation exceeds 0.15 or the slalom loses the line again, the track is over-responding and you should return to 0.12. If oval progress stays flat at 0.1175 with max_error still at the floor, turn authority is not the limit, and the next test is lower mass.
requested_changes: If the next race shows oval progress above 0.1175 and max_error below 0.06 with s-bend steering_oscillation at or below 0.15, keep wheel_track 0.10 and test the forward lead at y = 0.08 (the contract maximum) with the same spread and weights. Evidence: iteration 3 showed the lead moved s-bend progress from 0.04 to 0.165 and slalom from 0.03 to 0.1075.

If the next race shows s-bend steering_oscillation above 0.15 with completion still zero, or any slalom line loss, return wheel_track to 0.12 and set the lead to y = 0.06. Evidence: iteration 3 s-bend oscillation was 0.144 and slalom had one line loss at y = 0.07, so a narrower track is the likely cause of further jitter.

If oval progress stays at 0.1175 with max_error at about 0.06 at wheel_track 0.10, set mass to 0.6 to lower yaw inertia (mass times (body_length² + body_width²)/12) and make turn response quicker, keeping the other fields fixed. Evidence: oval steering_oscillation was only 0.074 in iteration 3, well below the 0.10 limit, so there is room for a more responsive robot on that track.
